Pulmonary consolidation can be referred to as the filling of alveolar spaces with fluid, pus, blood, or other substances, leading to increased lung tissue density. On a chest radiograph, signs of consolidation include:
1. A homogeneous opacity obscuring blood vessels, "air bronchograms" where air-filled bronchi appear as dark lines within the consolidation.
2. Loss of the normal lung-soft tissue interface ("silhouette sign"), and
3. No significant volume loss in the affected area, usually with poorly defined margins, often seen in a lobar distribution due to pneumonia.

prompts: How to identify the location of consolidation:
answerLines: Key points about consolidation on chest X-ray:
Appearance: A dense, hazy area with a relatively uniform opacity. 
Air bronchograms: The most characteristic sign, where air-filled bronchi appear  as dark lines within the consolidated area.
Silhouette sign: Loss of the normal border between the lung and adjacent  structures like the heart or diaphragm due to consolidation in that area.
No volume loss: Unlike lung collapse, consolidation does not usually cause a  visible decrease in lung volume.
Upper lobe consolidation: May obscure the aortic arch on the left side. 
Middle lobe consolidation: May obscure the right heart border.
Lower lobe consolidation: May obscure the diaphragm.
Tuberculosis (TB) – Primary or post-primary TB with focal consolidation 
Lymphoma – Can present as a localized lung mass or diffuse consolidation 
Pulmonary infarction (from pulmonary embolism) – May show a wedge-shaped  opacity.
Pulmonary edema – Cardiogenic or non-cardiogenic (e.g., ARDS). 
Pulmonary hemorrhage syndromes (e.g., Goodpasture's syndrome, Vasculitis) 
Radiation pneumonitis – Consolidation in previously irradiated lung fields 
Air bronchograms – More common in infectious causes.
Cavitation – Seen in TB, abscesses, fungal infections.
Peripheral consolidation – Seen in eosinophilic pneumonia, cryptogenic  organizing pneumonia.
Upper lobe involvement – TB, sarcoidosis, fungal infections.
Multifocal/migratory consolidations – Organizing pneumonia, eosinophilic  pneumonia.
